OpenAMRobot 2.0 · Hardware architecture

BOM Issue 7 · Reviewed diagram · 27 September 2026 · Balanced physical layout · Jetson / STM32 focus · Connection model, not a pin-released schematic

Superseded LiDAR, P-03 revision 18.4 item 13 (3 October 2026): the navigation LiDAR NAV-001 is the SLAMTEC RPLIDAR S3 (S3M1-R2), connected to the Jetson over USB through a USB to UART adapter and powered from the regulated 5 V rail (4.9 to 5.2 V, ripple at most 150 mV, start current 1.2 A, running 0.45 A typical). It replaces the RPLIDAR A1 of the existing robot and supersedes the Hokuyo UST-10LX of this BOM issue; the separately fused 24 V LiDAR branch (F-LIDAR) and the LiDAR Ethernet link are withdrawn, and there is no 12 V rail. Mounting: existing A1 bracket plus a spacer plate, scan plane at the A1 scan-plane height, lidar_link unchanged; scan window fully open, no translucent cover. Functional sensing only, not a safety device. Backup: RPLIDAR S2E, only if the S3 is unavailable. Only labels are updated: line geometry and the embedded Issue 7 source rows are unchanged until the next BOM issue is generated, and the S3 5 V supply and USB link are not drawn.

Reading the model

Solid: selected architecture. Dashed: conditional or alternative route. Grey: mounting or kit allocation. TBD: source does not release the detail.

Each branch fuse is explicit. Functional nodes such as K1/K2 split one BOM allocation; they are not additional purchases. Kit contents stay associated with their parent.

USB A/B/C are provisional logical allocations, not verified physical J401 port names. Power examples require engineering release.
